session.why: /subscribe/success is in PUBLIC_PATHS because Stripe redirects a sessionless mobile-handoff visitor here; the lock pins it public alongside /subscribe and /subscribe/cancel.

disclosure.why: The page is anon-reachable, but the one field it reads is only ever returned to a caller who already holds a session for that profile — a sessionless visitor receives 401 and the field is never projected.

checks.why: The page is anon but the contract it polls is authenticated — the 401 arm must stop immediately on the first attempt, or a sessionless mobile-handoff visitor burns twelve seconds on a poll that can never resolve.
The confirmed copy may only render when subscription_status is in {active, admin_managed} as returned by the server; the webhook owns activation and this page must never assert it from a timer.
Six polls at two seconds is a twelve-second ceiling; an unbounded poll on a page a paying user sits on is how a spinner becomes permanent.

errors.why: There is deliberately no error state: a transient network failure is swallowed inside the loop so polling continues, and the terminal copy says "active shortly" rather than claiming a failure the webhook may be seconds from resolving.

Activation truth lives in the Stripe webhook; this page only observes. MEASURED 2026-09-15. WIZARD_STEP fields, recorded here because the schema declares no wizard block: step 2 of 2; advances_on = a profile whose subscription_status is in {active, admin_managed}; resume_key = none; skip_when = the first poll returns 401 (the sessionless mobile-handoff visitor, for whom the app is the confirmation surface per Spec 96 §6); terminal = true.
